title: Fruta fresca en la plaza de Medellín

dialogue.speaker: Camila
dialogue.spanish: ¡Quiubo, parcero! Mirá qué lulos tan bonitos tienen en este puesto de la plaza.
dialogue.english: What's up, buddy! Look how nice the lulo fruits are at this market stall.

slang.example: Ese man es mi parcero desde el colegio.

dialogue.speaker: Sebastián
dialogue.spanish: ¡Están una chimba! Llevemos una bolsa para hacer jugo frío en la casa.
dialogue.english: They look amazing! Let's get a bag to make cold juice at home.

slang.example: ¡El concierto de anoche estuvo una chimba!

dialogue.speaker: Camila
dialogue.spanish: La señora dice que la docena vale ocho mil pesos y nos regala dos maracuyás de ñapa.
dialogue.english: The lady says a dozen costs eight thousand pesos and she'll throw in two passion fruits as a free bonus.

slang.actualMeaning: as a free extra / baker's dozen bonus at a market
slang.example: Compré tres empanadas y me dieron una más de ñapa.

dialogue.speaker: Sebastián
dialogue.spanish: ¡De una! Pagá vos en efectivo que yo te invito las arepas de queso ahorita.
dialogue.english: Let's do it! You pay in cash and I'll treat you to cheese corn cakes right now.

questions.question: Why do Camila and Sebastián want to buy 'lulos' at the Medellín market?
options: To make cold juice at home
To bring them to their office party
To sell them at their own restaurant
questions.explanation: Sebastián says: 'Llevemos una bolsa para hacer jugo frío en la casa.'

questions.question: How much does a dozen cost, and what does the vendor include for free?
options: 8,000 pesos plus two free passion fruits ('dos maracuyás de ñapa')
10,000 pesos plus a glass of orange juice
questions.explanation: Camila says: 'la docena vale ocho mil pesos y nos regala dos maracuyás de ñapa.'

questions.question: What does Sebastián offer to buy for Camila if she pays cash at the fruit stand?
questions.explanation: Sebastián says: 'Pagá vos en efectivo que yo te invito las arepas de queso ahorita.'

questions.question: Slang Side Quest: In Colombian Spanish, what do 'parcero', 'una chimba', and 'de ñapa' mean?
options: 'Parcero' = friend/buddy; 'una chimba' = amazing/cool; 'de ñapa' = as a free bonus
'Parcero' = vendor; 'una chimba' = expensive; 'de ñapa' = on credit
'Parcero' = neighbor; 'una chimba' = heavy; 'de ñapa' = in a bag
questions.explanation: In Colombia, 'parcero' means friend/buddy, 'una chimba' means awesome/amazing, and 'de ñapa' is a free extra thrown in by a vendor!
